title: What the Foot Can Push With: The Leg Jacobian, the Joint Torques That Hold a Body Up, and Why a Bent Knee Costs More Than a Straight One

artifact.note: the leg's Jacobian (how the foot moves when each joint does), the joint torques that make the ground push the foot up with a given force (minus the Jacobian's transpose times the force the ground gives), the foot's force from measured torques (the inverse), the joint rates for a foot velocity (and when they cannot be found), and the torques a quadruped's legs need to stand at different heights
